transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have the greenlight meeting today regarding the airline license for the independent concert documentary. The buyer's draft proposes a worldwide, twelve-month, non-exclusive license using the current picture and delivery master. Before I can sign off, I need each of you — rights, music, and post-production leads — to report your approval conditions. Let's start with the rights lead. Are there any rights clearance issues or conditions we need to address?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I reviewed the executed performer agreements yesterday. They restrict licensing of the documentary to the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom only, for a six-month non-exclusive term. The agreements also require a written rights amendment before delivery. The buyer's draft proposing a worldwide, twelve-month license exceeds those limitations.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a music clearance condition. I checked the publisher's clearance ledger this morning, and the current cut's use of the song 'Afterglow Avenue' lacks the synchronization clearance required for airline distribution. The cleared replacement is 'Night Transit.' I haven't updated the music cue sheet yet because the final territory and term were still unsettled, but before delivery we'll need to confirm the replacement and finalize the cue sheet accordingly.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I completed the airline's ingest test with the delivery vendor today. The airline requires a 1080p SDR master with stereo Lt/Rt audio and English SDH captions delivered as a sidecar VTT file. Our current 4K master uses a different audio and caption package, so I cannot approve delivery as-is. I have not yet issued the revised export order because the licensing terms are still pending. My condition for approval is that we authorize and complete a new export conforming to the airline's required spec before any delivery.
transcript.speaker: A4
